answers.explanation: Variable Length Subnet Masks: different subnets of one network get different masks.
Largest first keeps every block on a boundary that suits it. Small blocks fill in afterwards.
2² − 2 = 2. (RFC 3021 also allows a /31, but /30 is the classic answer.)
A /28 must start on a multiple of 16. 10.1.1.8 AND 255.255.255.240 gives 10.1.1.0.
The /26 ends at .191. The next free multiple of 16 is .192. (.160 overlaps the /26, .200 isn't a multiple of 16.)
A /30 is 4 addresses: .4 network, .5 and .6 hosts, .7 broadcast.
VLSM needs a routing protocol that carries masks: RIPv2, OSPF, EIGRP, or BGP.
Small subnets get small blocks, so space isn't wasted on a two-host link.
